title: EPA 609 practice test
description: Free EPA Section 609 motor vehicle air conditioning practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 40 CFR Part 82 (Subparts B and G) it comes from.

questions.question: A mechanic is paid to replace a car's water pump and does no work on the air conditioning refrigerant circuit. Under 40 CFR 82.30(b), do the Subpart B motor vehicle air conditioner rules apply to that job?

options.A: Yes, because they cover every paid repair on a motor vehicle
options.B: No, because the service does not involve the refrigerant in the motor vehicle air conditioner
options.C: Yes, whenever the vehicle is equipped with an air conditioner
options.D: Yes, but only if the mechanic works at a new-car dealership

questions.explanation: Subpart B applies to "any person performing service on a motor vehicle for consideration when this service involves the refrigerant in the motor vehicle air conditioner." Being paid is only half of the test; a job that never touches the refrigerant is outside it.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.30, Purpose and scope (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.32(b), who certifies equipment as "approved refrigerant recycling equipment" meeting one of the standards in § 82.36?

options.A: Any repair shop that has used the equipment for a year
options.B: The equipment's manufacturer, by its own declaration
options.C: The EPA Administrator or an organization approved under § 82.38
options.D: The state agency that registers motor vehicles

questions.explanation: Approved refrigerant recycling equipment means "equipment certified by the Administrator or an organization approved under § 82.38 as meeting either one of the standards in § 82.36." A manufacturer's own claim, a shop's experience or a state vehicle agency is not named.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.32(e)(1), "properly using" equipment means using it in conformity with the Subpart B regulations. Which of these does the definition expressly include?

options.A: The repair shop's own pricing policy for refrigerant work
options.B: Whatever procedure the vehicle owner asks for
options.C: The recommended service procedures and practices for the containment of refrigerant set forth in § 82.36(a) and the appendices to Subpart B
options.D: The state's vehicle emissions inspection schedule

questions.explanation: Properly using includes "the prohibitions and required practices set forth in § 82.34, and the recommended service procedures and practices for the containment of refrigerant set forth in § 82.36(a) and appendices A, B, C, D, E, and F to this subpart, as applicable." Pricing, owner requests and inspection schedules are not part of the definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A facility is paid to top off motor vehicle air conditioners (MVACs) with refrigerant and does no other refrigerant service. Under 40 CFR 82.32(e)(4), what equipment rule applies to it?

options.A: It must purchase approved refrigerant recycling equipment
options.B: It needs no equipment because it never removes refrigerant
options.C: It needs equipment only if it also services MVAC-like appliances
options.D: It must rent approved equipment only on days it does top-offs

questions.explanation: Top-off-only facilities are "subject to any and all requirements" that apply to wider refrigerant servicing, and "for facilities that charge MVACs, this includes the requirement to purchase approved refrigerant recycling equipment." Doing only top-offs is not an exemption.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A facility only charges MVAC-like appliances with refrigerant (top-offs) and does no other refrigerant service. Under 40 CFR 82.32(e)(4), which requirement applies to it?

options.A: It must purchase approved refrigerant recycling equipment, but no certification is needed
options.B: It must be properly trained and certified by a program approved under § 82.40 or § 82.161(a)(5)
options.C: Nothing, because top-offs of MVAC-like appliances are exempt
options.D: It only needs to keep a log of refrigerant purchases

questions.explanation: For facilities that only charge MVAC-like appliances, the rule "does not include the requirement to purchase approved refrigerant recycling equipment, but does include the requirement to be properly trained and certified." So an answer that drops certification is wrong. A separate paragraph, § 82.32(e)(5), says all persons opening MVAC-like appliances "must have at least one piece of approved recovery or recycling equipment available at their place of business"; "opening" is defined in § 82.152, not in Subpart B.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which vehicle falls outside EPA's definition of a "motor vehicle" in Subpart B?

options.A: A light duty delivery van
options.B: A heavy duty truck used on highways
options.C: A vehicle whose final assembly has not been completed by the original equipment manufacturer
options.D: A passenger car owned by a private person

questions.explanation: The definition "does not include a vehicle where final assembly of the vehicle has not been completed by the original equipment manufacturer." Passenger cars, light duty vehicles and heavy duty vehicles are named as included.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: EPA's definition of "motor vehicle air conditioners" in 40 CFR 82.32(d) describes them as which kind of equipment?

options.A: Mechanical vapor compression refrigeration equipment used to cool the driver's or passenger's compartment
options.B: Thermoelectric cooling modules mounted in the dashboard
options.C: Absorption refrigeration equipment driven by engine exhaust heat
options.D: Evaporative coolers that spray water into the incoming air

questions.explanation: Motor vehicle air conditioners means "mechanical vapor compression refrigeration equipment used to cool the driver's or passenger's compartment of any motor vehicle." The definition names vapor compression, not absorption, thermoelectric or evaporative cooling.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Subpart B, since November 15, 1995, what does the term "refrigerant" include besides class I and class II substances used in an MVAC?

options.A: Only HCFC-22
options.B: Engine coolant and antifreeze
options.C: Any substitute substance
options.D: Nothing else; substitutes are never covered

questions.explanation: Refrigerant means any class I or class II substance used in an MVAC, and "effective November 15, 1995, refrigerant shall also include any substitute substance." Substitutes are covered, so the answer saying they never are is wrong.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which business is a "motor vehicle disposal facility" under Subpart B?

options.A: A collision repair shop
options.B: A dealership's service department
options.C: A scrap yard that crushes vehicles with MVACs
options.D: A mobile repair van that services MVACs

questions.explanation: A motor vehicle disposal facility is a commercial facility engaged in disposal, which "includes dismantling, crushing or recycling," such as scrap yards. "Motor vehicle repair and/or servicing facilities, including collision repair facilities, are not considered motor vehicle disposal facilities."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A shop is paid to replace a leaking hose on a car's air conditioner that still holds refrigerant, a job during which discharge of refrigerant from the MVAC can reasonably be expected. Under 40 CFR 82.32(e)(2), when must approved equipment be used to extract the refrigerant?

options.A: Only after the old hose has been removed from the system
options.B: Only if the system still holds more than half of its charge
options.C: Never, because the leaking hose has already released refrigerant
options.D: Before the service is performed

questions.explanation: Section 82.32(e)(2) says "approved equipment must be used to extract refrigerant prior to performing any service during which discharge of refrigerant from the motor vehicle air conditioner can reasonably be expected." It adds that "Intentionally venting or disposing of refrigerant to the atmosphere is an improper use of equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A shop uses equipment that only recovers refrigerant (it does not recycle). What must the shop do with the recovered refrigerant to be "properly using" the equipment?

options.A: Store it indefinitely in the recovery tank
options.B: Recycle it on-site or send it off-site for reclamation
options.C: Put it straight back into the vehicle
options.D: Sell it to any buyer who asks

questions.explanation: For recover-only equipment, "properly using includes the requirement to recycle the refrigerant on-site or send the refrigerant off-site for reclamation." Putting it straight back skips the required recycling or reclamation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may MVAC refrigerant be recycled off-site (rather than reclaimed)?

options.A: Whenever any other repair shop that owns recycling equipment agrees to do it
options.B: Only if it was extracted with recover-only equipment and is then recycled off-site by equipment owned by the person who owns the recover-only equipment and owns or operates the establishment where it was extracted
options.C: Whenever a certified technician signs a transfer form
options.D: Only on the same day the refrigerant was extracted

questions.explanation: Refrigerant "may be recycled off-site only if" it was extracted with recover-only equipment and recycled "by equipment owned by the person that owns both the recover only equipment and owns or operates the establishment" where it was extracted. An unrelated shop's equipment does not meet that ownership condition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician certified under § 82.34(a)(2) buys refrigerant whose sale is restricted under Subpart F. It was extracted from an MVAC bound for disposal at a motor vehicle disposal facility and was not reclaimed. Under § 82.34(d)(2), how may the technician re-use it?

options.A: Only after selling it back to the disposal facility
options.B: In any refrigeration or air conditioning appliance, as long as it is used within one year
options.C: In any MVAC exactly as it came from the disposal facility
options.D: Only in an MVAC or MVAC-like appliance, and only if it has been reclaimed or properly recycled

questions.explanation: The paragraph says such a technician "may subsequently re-use such refrigerant only in an MVAC or MVAC-like appliance, and only if it has been reclaimed or properly recycled." Using it as-is, or in other kinds of appliances, does not meet both conditions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.34(e), when may refrigerant handling equipment manufactured or imported for use during the maintenance, service or repair of MVACs for consideration be introduced into interstate commerce?

options.A: Whenever it is labeled for professional use
options.B: After it has been used in the field for one year
options.C: Only if it meets the requirements of § 82.36
options.D: Whenever the importer pays a registration fee

questions.explanation: Such equipment "cannot be introduced into interstate commerce unless meeting the requirements of § 82.36." A label, field use or a fee does not replace meeting the equipment standards.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Refrigerant is recovered from an MVAC bound for disposal at a motor vehicle disposal facility, using approved refrigerant recycling equipment dedicated for use with MVACs and MVAC-like appliances. It will not be reclaimed. Under § 82.34(d)(1)(ii)(B), what must happen before it is charged into another MVAC?

options.A: Nothing; it may be charged into another MVAC as recovered
options.B: It must be returned to the company that originally produced it
options.C: It must be inspected at an EPA regional office
options.D: It must be recycled by the facility that charges or recharges it, properly using approved refrigerant recycling equipment

questions.explanation: The refrigerant must be "Subsequently recycled by the facility that charges or recharges the refrigerant into an MVAC or MVAC-like appliance, properly using approved refrigerant recycling equipment in accordance with any applicable recommended service procedures set forth in the appendices to this subpart B." Recovery alone is not enough.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the SAE J1990 equipment specification in Appendix A, how must CFC-12 (R-12) recycling equipment deal with noncondensable gases (NCGs)?

options.A: It must automatically purge NCGs if the acceptable level is exceeded, or have a device that alerts the operator that the NCG level has been exceeded
options.B: It must release all refrigerant along with the NCGs at the end of each job
options.C: It may ignore NCGs, because only moisture matters
options.D: It must ship every container with NCGs to a reclaimer

questions.explanation: "The equipment shall either automatically purge noncondensables (NCGs) if the acceptable level is exceeded or incorporate a device to alert the operator that NCG level has been exceeded." NCG removal "must be part of normal operation of the equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician takes the shop's approved refrigerant recycling equipment to a customer's location to service an MVAC there. What does the rule say?

options.A: This is allowed, and the service must meet all Subpart B requirements that would apply on-site
options.B: Approved equipment may never leave the shop
options.C: This is allowed, and on-site recordkeeping rules no longer apply
options.D: This is allowed only for top-offs

questions.explanation: Approved refrigerant recycling equipment "may be transported off-site" for service at other locations, and that servicing "must meet all of the requirements of this subpart B that would apply if the servicing occurred on-site." Moving off-site does not relax any requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What equipment must a person who opens MVAC-like appliances have available at their place of business?

options.A: None, if the technician is certified
options.B: At least one piece of approved recovery or recycling equipment
options.C: Access to a neighboring shop's equipment by written agreement
options.D: Equipment only if they open more than ten appliances a year

questions.explanation: Section 82.32(e)(5) says all persons opening (as defined in § 82.152) MVAC-like appliances "must have at least one piece of approved recovery or recycling equipment available at their place of business." Certification does not replace this, and the rule sets no yearly count.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.34(c), when may a technician training program issue certificates?

options.A: Only if the program complies with all of the standards in § 82.40(a)
options.B: Once it has trained at least 100 technicians
options.C: Whenever a technician pays the program's fee
options.D: Once a state licensing board has reviewed its test

questions.explanation: "No technician training programs may issue certificates unless the program complies with all of the standards in § 82.40(a)." Those standards cover training, test subject material, test administration and proof of certification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A buyer who is not certified under § 82.40 wants to buy small cans (under 20 pounds) of a class I or class II refrigerant suitable for MVACs. When may a seller sell to this buyer?

options.A: When the buyer says the refrigerant is for their own car
options.B: When the buyer shows a driver's license
options.C: When the buyer intends the containers for resale only and so certifies to the seller
options.D: When the buyer buys a full case of cans

questions.explanation: Sales of these small containers are allowed only to a person who is "properly trained and certified under § 82.40 or intended the containers for resale only, and so certifies to the seller." Personal use is not an exception.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: As a promotion, a parts store gives away a 12-ounce can of CFC-12 refrigerant, free, to a customer who is not certified under § 82.40 and is not buying for resale. Does § 82.34(b) reach this giveaway?

options.A: No, because no money changed hands
options.B: No, because cans holding less than one pound are exempt
options.C: No, because the rule regulates only the person who receives the can
options.D: Yes, because the paragraph covers distributing such containers, not only selling them

questions.explanation: Section 82.34(b) says "no person may sell or distribute, or offer for sale or distribution" such refrigerant in "a container which contains less than 20 pounds of such refrigerant to any person unless that person is properly trained and certified under § 82.40 or intended the containers for resale only." A free can is still distributed, and a 12-ounce can is well under 20 pounds.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: At a motor vehicle disposal facility, refrigerant from an MVAC bound for disposal is recovered with approved refrigerant recycling equipment dedicated for use with MVACs and MVAC-like appliances, to be recycled later by the facility that recharges it. Who may do this recovery?

options.A: Only an EPA inspector
options.B: Only the facility that will later recharge the refrigerant
options.C: Only a technician employed by a reclamation facility
options.D: A certified technician, or an employee, owner, or operator of, or contractor to, the disposal facility

questions.explanation: The recovery may be done "either by a technician certified under paragraph (a)(2) of this section, or by an employee, owner, or operator of, or contractor to, the disposal facility." The disposal facility's own staff are allowed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Refrigerant whose sale is restricted under Subpart F is extracted from an MVAC bound for disposal at a motor vehicle disposal facility and is not reclaimed. Who may it be sold to before re-use?

options.A: Anyone who pays for it
options.B: Any business holding a resale certificate
options.C: Only a technician certified under § 82.34(a)(2)
options.D: Any other disposal facility

questions.explanation: Such refrigerant "may be sold prior to its subsequent re-use only to a technician certified under paragraph (a)(2) of this section." A resale certificate is not named as an option for this refrigerant.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.36(c), how does the EPA Administrator maintain the list of approved refrigerant handling equipment?

options.A: By the name of each repair shop that owns the equipment
options.B: By manufacturer and model
options.C: By the state where the equipment was sold
options.D: By the price of the equipment

questions.explanation: "The Administrator will maintain a list of approved equipment by manufacturer and model." The list is not organized by owner, state or price.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A machine recovers, but does not recycle, a single, specific MVAC refrigerant that is not CFC-12, HFC-134a or HFO-1234yf. Under 40 CFR 82.36(a)(7), which standards must it meet?

options.A: Appendix F of Subpart B
options.B: Appendix A of Subpart B
options.C: Appendix E of Subpart B
options.D: Appendix H of Subpart G

questions.explanation: "Equipment that recovers but does not recycle refrigerants other than CFC-12, HFC-134a, and HFO-1234yf must meet the standards set forth in appendix F of this subpart." Appendix A covers CFC-12 recover-and-recycle equipment and Appendix E covers CFC-12 and HFC-134a equipment using common circuitry.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these is one of the ways an EPA-approved MVAC technician program may provide its training?

options.A: A signed note from the shop owner in place of training
options.B: A registration fee paid in place of training
options.C: Self-study of instructional material
options.D: Taking the test with no training offered

questions.explanation: Programs must provide training "through one or more of the following means: on-the-job training, training through self-study of instructional material, or on-site training involving instructors, videos or a hands-on demonstration." A fee or a signed note is not one of the listed means of training.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which subject must the certification tests of an approved MVAC technician program cover?

options.A: Engine tune-up procedures
options.B: The environmental consequences of refrigerant release and the effects of ozone layer depletion
options.C: Retail pricing of refrigerant
options.D: Shop insurance requirements

questions.explanation: The tests must cover "the environmental consequences of refrigerant release and the adverse effects of stratospheric ozone layer depletion," along with the service standards, future developments and the section 609 requirements. Engine tune-ups, pricing and insurance are not on the list.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who may grade a completed MVAC technician certification test?

options.A: An entity or individual who receives no benefit based on the outcome (a grading fee is allowed)
options.B: An instructor who is paid a bonus for each passing score
options.C: The technician who took the test
options.D: Anyone at all, as long as no fee is charged

questions.explanation: Tests "must be graded by an entity or individual who receives no benefit based on the outcome of testing; a fee may be charged for grading." A bonus for passing scores is a benefit based on the outcome, and charging no fee does not make any grader acceptable.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must each MVAC certification test provide about the person taking it?

options.A: A means of verifying the identification of the individual taking the test
options.B: A photo of the technician's vehicle
options.C: A letter from a vehicle manufacturer
options.D: Proof of two years of work experience

questions.explanation: "Each test must provide a means of verifying the identification of the individual taking the test." The rule does not ask for work experience, vehicle photos or manufacturer letters.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician takes an MVAC certification test with the help of a translator. What must the certificate show?

options.A: That the certificate is temporary
options.B: Nothing different; the certificate looks the same
options.C: That translator assistance was required
options.D: That the test must be retaken in English

questions.explanation: "If a translator is used, the certificate received must indicate that translator assistance was required." Programs are "encouraged to make provisions for non-English speaking technicians," and the rule says nothing about a temporary certificate or an English retest.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must an approved MVAC certification program give a technician who passes the test?

options.A: Only a verbal confirmation from the instructor
options.B: Individual proof of certification, such as a certificate, wallet-sized card or display card
options.C: Proof only after one year of service work
options.D: Nothing; the program keeps the result private

questions.explanation: Each program "must offer individual proof of certification, such as a certificate, wallet-sized card, or display card, upon successful completion of the test." A verbal confirmation or a delay of a year does not meet that.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What number must an approved MVAC certification program provide for each certified technician?

options.A: A unique number for each certified technician
options.B: The shop's EPA region number
options.C: One shared number for all technicians at the same shop
options.D: The VIN of the first vehicle the technician services

questions.explanation: "Each certification program must provide a unique number for each certified technician." A number shared by a whole shop, a region number or a VIN is not unique to the technician.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where may authorized representatives of EPA require MVAC technicians to show they can properly recover and/or recycle refrigerant?

options.A: Only at an EPA regional office
options.B: On the business entity's premises
options.C: Only by a written exam sent by mail
options.D: Only at the training program's test site

questions.explanation: Authorized representatives "may require technicians to demonstrate on the business entity's premises their ability to perform proper procedures for recovering and/or recycling refrigerant." The rule names the business premises, not an EPA office or a test site.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: EPA revokes an MVAC technician's certificate after a failed demonstration. What must the technician do before servicing or repairing any motor vehicle air conditioner again?

options.A: Wait 30 days
options.B: Be recertified
options.C: Have the shop owner sign for the work
options.D: Pay a fee to the equipment manufacturer

questions.explanation: "Technicians whose certification is revoked must be recertified before servicing or repairing any motor vehicle air conditioners." Waiting, an owner's signature or a fee does not replace recertification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.40, Technician training and certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides naming the purchaser, the address and the equipment, the signed certification statement under 40 CFR 82.42(a)(1) must include a statement about the people the purchaser authorizes to perform service. What must it say about them?

options.A: That each of them has at least two years of motor vehicle air conditioning experience
options.B: That each of them was trained by the equipment's manufacturer
options.C: That each of them holds a state mechanic's license
options.D: That each individual authorized by the purchaser to perform service is properly trained and certified in accordance with § 82.40

questions.explanation: The certification "must also include a statement that the equipment will be properly used in servicing motor vehicle air conditioners, that each individual authorized by the purchaser to perform service is properly trained and certified in accordance with § 82.40, and that the information given is true and correct." Work experience, a state license or manufacturer training is not what the statement covers.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which equipment details must a shop's signed certification statement to EPA include?

options.A: The manufacturer name, model number, date of manufacture and serial number of the equipment
options.B: The names of the shop's customers
options.C: The equipment's purchase price
options.D: The brand of refrigerant the shop buys

questions.explanation: The statement sets forth "the manufacturer name and equipment model number, the date of manufacture, and the serial number of the equipment," along with the purchaser's name and the establishment's address. Price, customer names and refrigerant brand are not listed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A person owns approved refrigerant recycling equipment certified under 40 CFR 82.36(a)(2). What record must they keep about refrigerant sent off-site?

options.A: The license plate of every vehicle serviced
options.B: The daily outdoor temperature
options.C: The name and address of any facility to which refrigerant is sent
options.D: The price paid for each container

questions.explanation: The owner "must maintain records of the name and address of any facility to which refrigerant is sent." License plates, temperatures and prices are not part of this record.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What records about equipment operators must an owner of approved refrigerant recycling equipment keep?

options.A: Records showing that all persons authorized to operate the equipment are currently certified under 40 CFR 82.40
options.B: Each operator's home address
options.C: Each operator's weekly work hours
options.D: Each operator's driver's license number

questions.explanation: The owner "must retain records demonstrating that all persons authorized to operate the equipment are currently certified under § 82.40." The rule asks for proof of current certification, not home addresses, hours or license numbers.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An authorized representative of the EPA Administrator arrives at a business that services MVACs for consideration and presents credentials. Under 40 CFR 82.42(b)(5), what must the business do?

options.A: Allow entry onto its premises and give access to all records required under § 82.42
options.B: Refuse entry until a court order is shown
options.C: Allow entry but keep its records closed
options.D: Mail copies of its records to EPA within 90 days instead

questions.explanation: Such entities "must allow an authorized representative of the Administrator entry onto their premises (upon presentation of his or her credentials) and give the authorized representative access to all records required to be maintained pursuant to this section." Both entry and record access are required.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where must entities that service motor vehicle air conditioners for consideration keep their required records?

options.A: At the nearest EPA regional office
options.B: At the equipment manufacturer
options.C: On-site
options.D: At the technician's home

questions.explanation: "Entities which service motor vehicle air conditioners for consideration must keep these records on-site." The records are also opened to EPA's authorized representative on the premises, so sending them elsewhere does not meet the rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A person sells a class I or class II refrigerant suitable for MVAC use in a container of less than 20 pounds. Unless the buyer is purchasing for resale only, what must the seller do?

options.A: Verify that the purchaser is properly trained and certified under 40 CFR 82.40
options.B: Collect a deposit on the container
options.C: Have the buyer read the store's sign aloud
options.D: Check the buyer's vehicle registration

questions.explanation: The seller "must verify that the purchaser is properly trained and certified under § 82.40" and "must have a reasonable basis for believing that the information presented by the purchaser is accurate." A vehicle registration or deposit does not show certification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A buyer purchases small containers (less than 20 pounds) of class I or class II MVAC refrigerant for resale only. What must the seller obtain?

options.A: Nothing at all
options.B: A verbal promise that the containers will be resold
options.C: A copy of the purchaser's tax return
options.D: A written statement from the purchaser that the containers are for resale only, with the purchaser's name and business address

questions.explanation: For resale-only purchases, "the seller must obtain a written statement from the purchaser that the containers are for resale only and indicate the purchasers name and business address." A verbal promise is not a written statement, and the exception still requires paperwork.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A store makes retail sales of class I or class II MVAC refrigerant in containers of less than 20 pounds. Where must it display the required federal sign?

options.A: Only in the employee break room
options.B: Only on the store's website
options.C: Prominently, where sales of such containers occur
options.D: Only at the loading dock

questions.explanation: The seller "must prominently display a sign where sales of such containers occur." A break room, website or loading dock is not where customers buy the containers.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the sign required at retail sales of small containers of class I and class II MVAC refrigerant state?

options.A: It is a violation of federal law to sell containers of Class I and Class II refrigerant of less than 20 pounds of such refrigerant to anyone who is not properly trained and certified to operate approved refrigerant recycling equipment.
options.B: Refrigerant sales are limited to two containers per customer.
options.C: It is a violation of federal law to sell refrigerant to anyone under 18 years of age.
options.D: Customers must return empty containers to receive a deposit refund.

questions.explanation: The sign states: "It is a violation of federal law to sell containers of Class I and Class II refrigerant of less than 20 pounds of such refrigerant to anyone who is not properly trained and certified to operate approved refrigerant recycling equipment." The rule ties sales to certification, not to age, quantity limits or deposits.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.42, Certification, recordkeeping and public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Following Appendix A's checking procedure, a technician has already vented a small amount of vapor from the top of a stored container of recycled R-12 into the recycle equipment, but the container pressure still exceeds Table 1. What does the procedure call for next?

options.A: Use the refrigerant anyway, because venting has already been tried
options.B: Release the rest of the container's vapor to the atmosphere
options.C: Add virgin R-12 to the container and check it again
options.D: Recycle the entire contents of the container

questions.explanation: Step 5.7 reads: "If the container still exceeds the pressure shown on Table 1, the entire contents of the container shall be recycled." The refrigerant may be used only when the pressure is below the Table 1 values, and venting to the atmosphere is not part of the procedure.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the R-12 containment procedure in Appendix A, a manifold gage set is being disconnected from the vehicle's air-conditioning system. What should be done with the gage set hoses first?

options.A: Empty them into a disposable refrigerant can
options.B: Open the hose valves so the hoses empty to the air
options.C: Cap the hose ends and store them still charged
options.D: Attach them to the reclaim equipment to recover the refrigerant from the hoses

questions.explanation: "When the manifold gage set is disconnected from the air-conditioning system or when the center hose is moved to another device which cannot accept refrigerant pressure, the gage set hoses should first be attached to the reclaim equipment to recover the refrigerant from the hoses." The procedure also says recycled refrigerant "should not be salvaged or stored in disposable refrigerant containers."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix A, a near-empty disposable R-12 container is attached to the recovery unit so the remaining refrigerant can be removed before the container is thrown away. When can the container valve be closed?

options.A: After the recovery unit has run for one minute, whatever the container pressure
options.B: When the container has been reduced from a pressure to a vacuum
options.C: Before the recovery unit is started, so no air enters it
options.D: As soon as the container feels cold to the touch

questions.explanation: Step 8.2 reads: "Attach the container to the recovery unit and remove the remaining refrigerant. When the container has been reduced from a pressure to a vacuum, the container valve can be closed." Then "The container should be marked empty and is ready for disposal."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix A's procedure for checking a stored container of recycled R-12 for excess noncondensable gases, where is the air temperature measured?

options.A: Outdoors, in the shade
options.B: Within 4 in (10 cm) of the container surface
options.C: Inside the passenger compartment of the vehicle
options.D: At the shop's wall thermostat

questions.explanation: The step reads: "With a calibrated thermometer, measure the air temperature within 4 in (10 cm) of the container surface." The pressure is read with "a calibrated pressure gage, with 1 psig divisions."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the SAE J1990 equipment specification in Appendix A, why must the equipment's lubricant measuring system take into account refrigerant dissolved in the lubricant sample?

options.A: Dissolved refrigerant makes the sample look smaller than it is, so the vehicle would get too little lubricant
options.B: Dissolved refrigerant raises the moisture limit of the recycled refrigerant
options.C: Dissolved refrigerant creates the illusion that more lubricant has been recovered than actually has been, which could lead to overcharging the vehicle system with lubricant
options.D: Dissolved refrigerant must be counted so the shop can bill the customer for it

questions.explanation: Item 7.7 says "Refrigerant dissolves in lubricant sample. This creates the illusion that more lubricant has been recovered than actually has been." The measuring system must account for it "to prevent overcharging the vehicle system with lubricant."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the R-12 recovery procedure in Appendix A, once recovery from the vehicle is complete, what is done before proceeding with the repair?

options.A: Remove the service lines first, then close their valves
options.B: Leave the service lines connected with valves open during the repair
options.C: Vent the refrigerant left in the service lines
options.D: Close the valves in the service lines, then remove the service lines from the vehicle system

questions.explanation: The step reads: "Close the valves in the service lines and then remove the service lines from the vehicle system. Proceed with the repair/service." Removing the lines before closing the valves reverses that order.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.170(a), what is the purpose of the SNAP regulations in Subpart G?

options.A: To implement section 609 of the Clean Air Act on technician certification for motor vehicle air conditioner service
options.B: To set the sign that stores must post where small cans of refrigerant are sold
options.C: To set the purity standard for recycled refrigerant returned to motor vehicle air conditioners
options.D: To implement section 612 of the Clean Air Act on the acceptability of substitutes for ozone-depleting compounds

questions.explanation: Section 82.170(a) says the purpose is "to implement section 612 of the Clean Air Act" regarding "the acceptability of substitutes for ozone-depleting compounds." Section 609 technician certification is handled in Subpart B, not in the SNAP program.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.170, Purpose and scope (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 40 CFR 82.172 define a "substitute" (or "alternative") under the SNAP program?

options.A: Any chemical, product substitute, or alternative manufacturing process, existing or new, intended for use as a replacement for a class I or II compound
options.B: Only a newly invented chemical that has never been sold before
options.C: Only a refrigerant that EPA has already listed as acceptable without conditions
options.D: Any mixture or blend of two or more compounds

questions.explanation: The definition covers "any chemical, product substitute, or alternative manufacturing process, whether existing or new, intended for use as a replacement for a class I or II compound." It is not limited to new chemicals ("whether existing or new"), and "any mixture or blend of two or more compounds" is the separate definition of "mixture."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.172, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.172, what are "use restrictions" on a substitute?

options.A: Limits on the price at which a substitute may be sold
options.B: Rules on who may take the technician certification test
options.C: Recordkeeping rules for shops that buy refrigerant in containers under 20 pounds
options.D: Conditions on how the substitute can be used across a sector end-use, or limits on the end-uses or specific applications where it can be used within a sector

questions.explanation: The rule defines use restrictions as restrictions imposing "either conditions on how the substitute can be used across a sector end-use or limits on the end-uses or specific applications where it can be used within a sector." The definition says nothing about price, testing or small-container sales records.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.172, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: EPA has listed a substitute as acceptable subject to use restrictions, and the rulemaking imposing them is in effect. What does 40 CFR 82.174(c) require of any person who uses that substitute?

options.A: Notify EPA within 90 days after first using it
options.B: Get the vehicle owner's written consent before using it
options.C: Adhere to any use restrictions set by the acceptability decision
options.D: Nothing, because use restrictions bind only the company that produces the substitute

questions.explanation: Section 82.174(c) says "No person may use a substitute without adhering to any use restrictions set by the acceptability decision" after the effective date of the rulemaking. It applies to any person who uses the substitute, so it is wrong to say only the producer is bound.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.174, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A rulemaking adds a substitute to the list of unacceptable substitutes. Under 40 CFR 82.174(d), when does the ban on using it apply?

options.A: Only after the person's current supply of the substitute runs out
options.B: After the effective date of the rulemaking adding it to the list
options.C: Only to people who bought the substitute after the listing
options.D: Only to the substitute's producer, not to the people who use it

questions.explanation: Section 82.174(d) says "No person may use a substitute after the effective date of any rulemaking adding such substitute to the list of unacceptable substitutes." The rule contains no exception for existing supply or earlier purchases.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.174, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A shop is offered a substitute refrigerant that it has reason to know was imported in violation of the Subpart G regulations. What does 40 CFR 82.174(b) say?

options.A: The shop may not use it
options.B: The shop may use it as long as it does not resell it
options.C: The shop may use it if it pays the import duty
options.D: The shop may use it until EPA sends a warning letter

questions.explanation: Section 82.174(b) says "No person may use a substitute which a person knows or has reason to know was manufactured, processed or imported in violation of the regulations in this subpart." The rule offers no exception for paying duties, not reselling, or waiting for a warning.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.174, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In Appendix B, which flammable substitutes are listed as unacceptable for CFC-12 motor vehicle air conditioners (retrofit and new equipment)?

options.A: Flammable substitutes other than R-152a or HFO-1234yf in new equipment
options.B: R-152a and HFO-1234yf in new equipment
options.C: Only flammable substitutes sold in cans under 20 pounds
options.D: Only flammable substitutes used by uncertified persons

questions.explanation: The table lists "Flammable Substitutes, other than R-152a or HFO-1234yf in new equipment" as "Unacceptable." EPA's comments in the table note that R-152a and HFO-1234yf "may be used in new equipment with the use conditions in appendix B," so listing them as unacceptable is wrong.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix B lists Hydrocarbon Blend B as unacceptable in CFC-12 motor vehicle air conditioners (retrofit and new equipment). What reason do EPA's comments in the table give?

options.A: It contains R-c318, a PFC with an extremely high GWP and lifetime
options.B: It contains HCFCs that deplete the ozone layer
options.C: Flammability is a serious concern, and data have not been submitted to show it can be used safely in this end-use
options.D: It requires recovery equipment that does not exist

questions.explanation: For Hydrocarbon Blend B, EPA's comment says "Flammability is a serious concern. Data have not been submitted to demonstrate it can be used safely in this end-use." The PFC (R-c318) reason is the comment for a different entry, R-405A.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In the Appendix B entry that lists HFO-1234yf as a CFC-12 substitute in automobile motor vehicle air conditioning, which equipment does the application cover?

options.A: Any vehicle, as long as the shop owns approved recovery equipment
options.B: Retrofit of existing CFC-12 systems in any vehicle
options.C: Household refrigerators and freezers
options.D: New equipment in passenger cars and light-duty trucks only

questions.explanation: The application column reads "New equipment in passenger cars and light-duty trucks only," and the decision is "Acceptable subject to use conditions." The entry does not cover retrofits of CFC-12 systems, and other Appendix B rows cover other kinds of new vehicles separately.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In the Appendix B HFO-1234yf use conditions (as of June 3, 2022), the use fitting with a 0.5-inch diameter, 16 threads per inch and a left thread direction is specified for connections with which containers?

options.A: Recovery cylinders on CFC-12 recycling equipment
options.B: CO2 refrigerant service containers
options.C: Small refrigerant cans for consumer or professional use
options.D: Containers of HFC-134a used to retrofit CFC-12 systems

questions.explanation: The condition reads: "For connections with small refrigerant cans for consumer or professional use, use fittings must have a diameter of 0.5 inches, a thread pitch of 16 thread per inch, and a left thread direction, consistent with SAE J2844." For containers used in professional servicing, a separate sentence says use fittings "must be consistent with SAE J2844," and CO2 service containers get a right-hand thread in the CO2 entry.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: As of June 3, 2022, HFO-1234yf MVAC systems must adhere to all of the safety requirements of SAE J639. Which item does the Appendix B condition name among those requirements?

options.A: A flammable refrigerant warning label
options.B: A refrigerant identifier built into each service port
options.C: A sight glass on the receiver-drier
options.D: A 5-pound maximum system charge

questions.explanation: The condition says the systems must meet SAE J639 "including requirements for a flammable refrigerant warning label, high-pressure compressor cutoff switch and pressure relief devices, and unique fittings." None of the other options is named in the condition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the HFO-1234yf use conditions in Appendix B (as of June 3, 2022), use fittings for connections with refrigerant containers for professional servicing must be consistent with which SAE standard?

options.A: SAE J1739
options.B: SAE J2844
options.C: SAE J2773
options.D: SAE J1052

questions.explanation: The condition says that for containers "for use in professional servicing, use fittings must be consistent with SAE J2844." SAE J1739 is the standard the conditions name for manufacturers' Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), not for container fittings.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under condition (2) for HFO-1234yf in Appendix B (as of June 3, 2022), who must conduct a Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) as provided in SAE J1739, and for what minimum period must it be kept on file?

options.A: Manufacturers, for at least one year from the date of creation
options.B: Service technicians, for at least three years after each repair
options.C: Manufacturers, for at least three years from the date of creation
options.D: Shop owners, for at least five years after buying the refrigerant

questions.explanation: Condition (2) says "Manufacturers must conduct Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA)" and "must keep the FMEA on file for at least three years from the date of creation." This condition binds manufacturers, not service technicians or shop owners.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What do EPA's comments in the Appendix B HFO-1234yf entries note about recharging MVAC systems with HFO-1234yf, consistent with EPA's Significant New Use Rule under the Toxic Substances Control Act?

options.A: Anyone may recharge any MVAC system with HFO-1234yf
options.B: Commercial users or consumers can only recharge MVAC systems with HFO-1234yf where the original charging with HFO-1234yf was done by the original equipment manufacturer
options.C: Only the original equipment manufacturer may ever recharge an HFO-1234yf system
options.D: HFO-1234yf may be used to top off a CFC-12 system

questions.explanation: EPA's comments in the table note that "commercial users or consumers can only recharge MVAC systems with HFO-1234yf where the original charging of the system with HFO-1234yf was done by the original equipment manufacturer." This is a comment pointing to a separate TSCA rule, not one of the SNAP use conditions, and it lets commercial users and consumers recharge such systems, so the option limiting recharging to the original equipment manufacturer is wrong.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: R-152a is acceptable subject to use conditions in new CFC-12 automobile MVAC equipment. Under the Appendix B condition, foreseeable leaks into the passenger compartment must not result in what?

options.A: Any measurable R-152a in the engine compartment
options.B: R-152a concentrations of 3.7% v/v or above in any part of the free space inside the passenger compartment for more than 15 seconds when the car ignition is on
options.C: R-152a concentrations of 10% v/v or above in the trunk for more than one hour
options.D: R-152a concentrations of 3.7% v/v or above only while the car is parked with the ignition off

questions.explanation: The condition requires engineering strategies and/or devices so that leaks "do not result in R-152a concentrations of 3.7% v/v or above in any part of the free space" inside the passenger compartment "for more than 15 seconds when the car ignition is on." The limit applies while the ignition is on, not while it is off. This condition is a design requirement for the vehicle system.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For R-152a in new CFC-12 automobile MVAC equipment, Appendix B says manufacturers must adhere to all the safety requirements of SAE Standard J639 (adopted 2011). Which items does the condition say those requirements include?

options.A: A high pressure system warning label and right-hand thread fittings
options.B: Barrier hoses and an "ozone depleter" label
options.C: A label with the technician's name and the date of the retrofit
options.D: Unique fittings and a flammable refrigerant warning label

questions.explanation: The R-152a condition names SAE J639 "including unique fittings and a flammable refrigerant warning label," as well as SAE Standard J2773. The high pressure system warning label is named in the CO2 entry, and the technician-name label is an Appendix D retrofit condition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix D, SNAP submissions for MVAC refrigerants must include fitting specifications, samples of all fittings and the detailed label, or the submission is considered incomplete. What does the appendix say about a substitute whose submission is incomplete?

options.A: It becomes acceptable automatically 90 days after it is submitted
options.B: It may be sold, but not used, while EPA reviews it
options.C: It may be used in retrofitted systems only
options.D: It may not be sold or used, regardless of other acceptability determinations

questions.explanation: "Under section 612 of the Clean Air Act, substitutes for which submissions are incomplete may not be sold or used, regardless of other acceptability determinations." The sale prohibition "will not end until 90 days after EPA determines the submission is complete," not 90 days after submission.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix B lists carbon dioxide (CO2) as acceptable subject to use conditions in new CFC-12 motor vehicle air conditioning equipment. Which label does the condition list by name?

options.A: A flammable refrigerant warning label
options.B: A high pressure system warning label
options.C: An "ozone depleter" label
options.D: A label with the price of the refrigerant charge

questions.explanation: The CO2 condition says its use must follow SAE J639 (2011 version) "including: Installation of a high pressure system warning label; Installation of a compressor cut-off switch" and unique fittings. The flammable refrigerant warning label is named in the R-152a and HFO-1234yf entries, not in the CO2 entry.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Appendix B use conditions for CO2 in new motor vehicle air conditioning equipment, what thread direction must the unique fitting for CO2 refrigerant service containers have?

options.A: Left-hand thread direction
options.B: Right-hand thread direction
options.C: Either direction, as long as the thread pitch differs from CFC-12
options.D: No thread; only quick-connect fittings are allowed

questions.explanation: The condition calls for an outside diameter of 20.955 mm (0.825 inches) "and righthand thread direction for CO2 refrigerant service containers." A table footnote adds that this container fitting requirement applies only to service containers used during MVAC servicing; the left thread direction is the HFO-1234yf small-can requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Appendix D use conditions for CFC-12 substitutes in MVACs, what must systems have to prevent discharge of refrigerant to the atmosphere?

options.A: A refrigerant identifier built into the service port
options.B: A sight glass on the receiver-drier
options.C: A second pressure relief valve that vents into the engine compartment
options.D: A device to limit compressor operation before the pressure relief device will vent refrigerant

questions.explanation: "In order to prevent discharge of refrigerant to the atmosphere, systems shall have a device to limit compressor operation before the pressure relief device will vent refrigerant." The aim is to stop the compressor before the relief device releases refrigerant.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A shop wants to use a CFC-12 substitute in MVACs with fittings designed by a third-party parts maker, not by the refrigerant's manufacturer. The fittings differ from those used with every other refrigerant. Under Appendix D, may it?

options.A: No; using a refrigerant with a fitting designed by anyone other than the refrigerant's manufacturer violates the use condition
options.B: Yes, because the fittings are unique to that refrigerant
options.C: Yes, if a certified technician installs them
options.D: Yes, if the fittings are used only on the shop's own equipment

questions.explanation: A refrigerant may only be used with fittings "specifically intended for that refrigerant and designed by the manufacturer of the refrigerant." "Using a refrigerant with a fitting designed by anyone else, even if it is different from fittings used with other refrigerants, is a violation of this use condition."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Appendix D use conditions, an existing CFC-12 service port is retrofitted with a conversion assembly. How must the assembly attach to the CFC-12 fitting?

options.A: Hand-tightened only, so it can be taken off if CFC-12 service is needed later
options.B: Through an adapter, so either refrigerant's equipment can connect
options.C: With a thread lock adhesive and/or a separate mechanical latching mechanism, in a manner that permanently prevents the assembly from being removed
options.D: With a push-on plastic cap over the old port

questions.explanation: "When existing CFC-12 service ports are retrofitted, conversion assemblies shall attach to the CFC-12 fitting with a thread lock adhesive and/or a separate mechanical latching mechanism in a manner that permanently prevents the assembly from being removed." The appendix also says "Using an adapter or deliberately modifying a fitting to use a different refrigerant is a violation of this use condition."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After a retrofit under Appendix D, some information about the previous refrigerant on the air conditioning system cannot be covered by the new label. What must be done with that information?

options.A: Leave it readable so later technicians know the system's history
options.B: Cover it with a removable sticker
options.C: Nothing, as long as the new label has a different background color
options.D: Render it permanently unreadable

questions.explanation: "Information on the previous refrigerant that cannot be covered by the new label must be rendered permanently unreadable." The label itself "must be affixed to the system over information related to the previous refrigerant, in a location not normally replaced during vehicle repair."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix D, a vehicle is retrofitted to a refrigerant that displays flammability limits as measured according to ASTM E681. Which statement must the retrofit label carry for that reason?

options.A: No statement, because flammability is shown only by the label color
options.B: "Caution—Should Be Operated By Qualified Personnel"
options.C: "High pressure system"
options.D: "This refrigerant is FLAMMABLE. Take appropriate precautions."

questions.explanation: If the refrigerant "displays flammability limits as measured according to ASTM E681," the label must carry the statement "This refrigerant is FLAMMABLE. Take appropriate precautions."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix H's criteria for unique fittings for alternative motor vehicle refrigerants, what makes two screw-on fittings "differ"?

options.A: Only the thread pitch is changed
options.B: The diameter differs by at least 1/16 inch, or the thread direction is reversed
options.C: The fittings are a different color
options.D: The fittings come from different manufacturers

questions.explanation: For screw-on fittings, "differ" means "either the diameter must differ by at least 1⁄16 inch or the thread direction must be reversed." The rule says "Simply changing the thread pitch is not sufficient."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart G, Appendix H (as of Nov 3, 2026)
